title: A shared first step for STX1B families and DEE-P Connections

sentences.text: STX1B and SNAP25 help nerve cells release messages, offering a reason to explore collaboration without assuming identical needs.
The atlas infers DEEP’s SNAP25 connection from a website link, with confidence 0.45, below 0.5; this is not confirmed membership.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: RARE-X, the Congenital Muscle Disease International Registry (CMDIR), and Simons Searchlight include SNAP25-related disorders and offer possible starting points for shared data collection.
The atlas suggests RARE-X may be reusable and the registries adaptable, but STX1B access needs confirmation.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Review both sides of the contested STX1B gain-of-function connection—the idea that a protein does too much—before using it to justify sharing resources.
Check atonic seizures, epileptic encephalopathy, focal impaired awareness seizures and the other symptom gaps; missing records do not establish absence.
The resource comparison also flags a SNAP25 mechanism in which an altered protein blocks the working protein.
Confirm RARE-X acceptance and registry adaptations; Searchlight enrols by genetic diagnosis, with SNAP25/VAMP2 coverage drawn from its website rather than the ClinicalTrials.gov condition list.
The related intervention study requires genetically confirmed congenital myasthenic syndromes, including SYT2 or SNAP25B deficiency; STX1B eligibility would need changing.
Check for an existing STX1B group and enrolment options before considering a new family network.
Let us jointly send SLC6A1 Connect one enquiry asking whether Simons Searchlight could include STX1B-related epilepsies.
Is there a dedicated STX1B patient organisation, an enrolling registry or natural history study, or an enrolling interventional trial?
Is an accessible animal or cell model documented in the atlas?
Which individual variants increase activity, impair the protein’s chemical activity, or cause loss of function?
Dear DEE-P Connections team,
I’m writing on behalf of families affected by STX1B-related epilepsies.
Could we explore a small collaboration?
Please join us in asking SLC6A1 Connect about STX1B inclusion in Simons Searchlight.
We would welcome your help checking eligibility and family priorities before going further.
Thank you for considering this request.
[Your name], on behalf of families affected by STX1B-related epilepsies
